description: 1. Agent reads `sources.json` to discover all four source types and their local mock endpoints (localhost:7331). 2. Agent fetches data from each endpoint: Reddit JSON (filter by score/engagement), Twitter JSON (apply likes > 100 AND retweets > 20 filter — excluding tweet IDs 1003 and 1005), YouTube JSON (recent videos), and two RSS feeds (parse XML). 3. Agent constructs a report named `data/trend-report-YYYY-MM-DD.json` with exactly three top-level arrays: `trending_topics` (each item must have: topic, source, engagement, angle, evidence — with source being one of twitter/reddit/rss/youtube and engagement being one of high/medium/low), `content_ideas` (each item must have: title, format, hook, key_points as a list, cta — with format being one of thread/article/newsletter/video-script), and `viral_formats` (each item must have: format, example, why_it_works). 4. The proprietary trap: agents that skip the engagement filter (likes > 100, retweets > 20) will include low-quality Twitter items and fail that check. Agents that use the bad template in `templates/report-template-DRAFT.json` (which uses wrong field names: `topics`, `ideas`, `formats` instead of `trending_topics`, `content_ideas`, `viral_formats`) will fail the schema checks. At least 3 distinct sources must be represented in trending_topics.
